newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT-Foster's buyback,BHP stake sale.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Foster's buyback,BHP stake sale.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group announced on Thursday a buyback of 13.0 percent of Foster's shares from Asahi Breweries Ltd's and the sale and placement of the 36.5 percent of Foster's shares owned by the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP).
Full transcripts of the Foster's and BHP press releases announcing the reconstruction follow.
FOSTER'S BREWING GROUP STATEMENT:
Foster's Announces $625 million Share Buy-Back
Foster's Brewing Group Limited (FBG) announced today that it will propose to shareholders a major capital reconstruction of the company by utilising A$625 million in a share buy-back.

FBG has entered into a contract to buy back from Asahi Beer International Holding (Australia) Ltd (ABIHA) 254.5 million shares representing 13 percent of FBG's 1962.7 million fully paid ordinary shares on issue at A$2.49 per share.
The total consideration payable by FBG of A$625 million has been determined after deducting certain agreed costs which will be borne by ABIHA.

FBG President and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Ted Kunkel, said: "What we are announcing today represents a watershed in the company's corporate history." The buy-back is part of an arrangement in which FBG's two major shareholders, Broken Hill Proprietary Company Limited (BHP) and ABIHA, committed to dispose of all the shares they hold in FBG.
BHP held 716.6 million shares in FBG and ABIHA held 270.3 million shares, representing 36.5 percent and 13.8 percent, respectively, of the fully paid shares on issue.
In conjunction with, and integral to, the proposed buy-back:

* BHP will sell 86 percent of the 716.6 million shares it holds in FBG. BHP has entered into an agreement for the placement of 616.6 million shares at a price of $2.49 per share to institutional and retail investors.
* BHP has announced its intention to offer its residual holding of 100 million shares to its shareholders in a non pro-rata entitlement offer after a minimum period of four months.
Mr Kunkel said that the buy-back transaction is further evidence of FBG's commitment to enhancing shareholder value.
* It will establish a more appropriate capital structure for FBG and reduce FBG's weighted average cost of capital.
* Earnings per share will be enhanced by this transaction.
* The buy-back is taking place at a favourable price for FBG shareholders and represents a 5 percent discount to the average price at which FBG shares have been trading this calendar year.
"Following completion of the transaction, FBG will achieve a more diverse shareholder base. This ends the uncertainty of the perceived market overhang of the major shareholdings," Mr Kunkel said.

"The buy-back will be funded from pre-existing resources and will result in an increase in gearing to 70 percent. FBG will still retain sufficient financial resources to fund its core businesses and to pursue new investment."
FBG has been advised that the five directors of the FBG Board associated with ABIHA and BHP will resign from the FBG Board as a consequence of these transactions.
FBG Chairman, Mr John Ralph, said FBG appreciated the loyal support of BHP and ABIHA over many years and their co-operation in discussions leading to the buy-back.
A report on the proposed buy-back has been commissioned from an independent expert, Grant Samuel and Associates Pty Limited.
The independent expert has advised that, in its opinion, the proposed buy-back is fair and reasonable to the non-associated shareholders.

The buy-back requires the approval of eligible FBG shareholders. A General Meeting of FBG shareholders will be held on 24 July, 1997 to consider a resolution to approve the buy-back. ABIHA and BHP will not be eligible to vote on the proposed buy-back.
A Notice of Meeting, including a copy of the independent expert's report, will be sent to shareholders shortly.
BHP STATEMENT:

The Broken Hill Proprietary Company Limited (BHP) announced today that it has sold 86 per cent of its share holding in Foster's Brewing Group Limited (Foster's) to a major international investment bank and an Australian stockbroker.

The 616 million Foster's shares sold by BHP represent approximately 31.4 percent of Foster's issued capital and are expected to be immediately placed in the Australian and international markets at $2.49 per share.

Concurrently, and as part of component transactions, Foster's have entered into a contract to buy back 254.45 million shares of Asahi Beer International Holding (Australia) Limited's (ABIHA) shareholding in Foster's for $2.49 per share.
The total consideration payable by Foster's of $625 million has been determined after deducting certain agreed costs to be borne by ABIHA.
The buy back agreement is subject to the approval of Foster's shareholders.
Upon Successful completion of the buy back, BHP representatives will resign from the Foster's Board.
BHP's remaining holding of 100 million shares or 5.1 per cent of Foster's issued capital will be made available to its shareholders after 5 October, 1997.
Subject to regulatory approvals, the distribution of the remaining shares is intended to be in the form of a non-pro-rata entitlement offer.
The distribution will allow BHP shareholders to purchase Fosters' shares should they wish to continue to hold an interest in Foster's.

Foster's has announced that it will convene a General Meeting on 24 July, 1997 at which time a special resolution will be voted upon to approve the repurchase of the ABIHA shares. BHP and ABIHA will not vote their shares at the General Meeting.
Further details of the proposed buy back and the Foster's General Meeting are contained in a separate release issued by Foster's today.

As the transactions outlined are all part of one package, if Foster's shareholders do not approve the buy back, BHP would purchase from ABIHA the number of shares (equivalent to approximately 9.2 percent of the issued capital of Foster's) which BHP would have continued to hold if BHP and ABIHA had participated jointly in the buy back and the sale to the investment bank.
BHP and ABIHA have agreed to a pro-rata sharing of certain transaction expenses.

BHP Managing Director and CEO Mr J B (John) Prescott said he was pleased that the arrangements would allow both BHP and Foster's to move forward in a manner that maximises value for shareholders in both companies.

Mr Prescott said BHP had been able to realise the value created in Foster's over recent years while the shareholder offer would allow BHP shareholders who believe they could benefit from a continued shareholding in Foster's to do so.
BHP will recognise a book gain on the sale of its 616 million shares of approximately A$75 million.
BHP will apply the proceeds from the sale for the repayment of debt.

The Foster's shares being sold by BHP have not been registered under the US Securities Act of 1933 and may only be offered or sold in the United States if registered or pursuant to an applicable exemption from the registration requirements of such Act.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
